html:
SMTO-BOOT-0039 — Your graphics card gave a wrong answer to a basic test

GUID: fa451b59-c0e2-42b3-8589-7ce1ebe7cb25
Slug: boot-cuda-kernel-failed
Domain: BOOT · Subsystem: boot

What happened

  • While checking the model environment, the installer asked each graphics card (GPU) to add 1 and 1 and got the wrong answer. Everything stays installed, but it isn't safe to run models with it yet.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Run nvidia-smi in a terminal and make sure every graphics card appears without error messages. A wrong result usually comes from a driver or hardware problem, and nvidia-smi often shows it.
  2. Update or reinstall the NVIDIA driver, restart the computer, then run ./src/vllm/install-vllm.sh --verify-only followed by your environment's name (vllm by default). This repeats the check without reinstalling anything, so you can see whether the driver change fixed it.
  3. Look at the last line starting with “GPU” before the error, and tell the person who manages this computer which card it names. The installer prints each card's name just before testing it, so that line shows which card failed.

What success looks like

  • The check finishes and prints “vLLM verification complete.”

If it still fails

  • Send the error code and the full terminal output to the person who maintains your model setup. Don't start model servers from this environment until the check passes; their answers could be wrong.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • install-vllm.sh verification ran torch.ones(1).add_(1) on a CUDA device and the scalar result was not 2, so final verification stopped with the environment and packages still installed.

What this means

  • Installed CUDA verification computes a small tensor addition but its scalar result is not the expected value 2. Final installed-environment verification stops after a tensor addition returns an unexpected scalar value. The environment and packages remain installed. This diagnostic does not identify which driver, hardware or installed binary caused the incorrect value. Exceptions raised by the kernel are separate failures.

Why this can happen

  • Installed CUDA verification computes a small tensor addition but its scalar result is not the expected value 2.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the selected GPU, driver and installed PyTorch build before serving workload traffic.

How to fix it

  • The last “GPU …:” line printed before the failure identifies the device. Check the driver with nvidia-smi (and Xid errors in dmesg), confirm the PyTorch CUDA build shown in the “vLLM …; PyTorch …; CUDA …” line supports this GPU and driver, update or reinstall the driver and reboot, then rerun ./src/vllm/install-vllm.sh --verify-only with the environment name until it completes. Do not serve models from the environment until it passes.
  • Inspect the driver, GPU and installed PyTorch CUDA build before serving a model.

Retry and execution caution

  • Diagnose the driver/GPU/PyTorch combination and require --verify-only to complete successfully before serving a model.

How to verify the fix

  • Verification in the selected environment returns 2 for the small CUDA addition on each selected GPU and completes all remaining checks.

What not to do

  • Do not remove retained state or weaken trust checks to make an unavailable dependency appear healthy.

Technical notes

  • Final installed-environment verification stops after a tensor addition returns an unexpected scalar value. The environment and packages remain installed.
  • This diagnostic does not identify which driver, hardware or installed binary caused the incorrect value. Exceptions raised by the kernel are separate failures.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
